data.what: Fixed the trivy red by bumping the digest-pinned base image (c45a22ea -> ed86c822) in BOTH Dockerfile stages, rather than adding '--only-upgrade libssh2-1' to the runtime apt line or waiving the finding in security-floors.txt
data.why: The finding was not the base image's fault and not this branch's: a cold 'apt-get install curl' against the OLD digest already resolves the fixed libssh2-1 1.10.0-3+deb12u1 from bookworm-security, so what shipped +b1 was security-scan.yml's cached BuildKit apt layer (scope key = requirements.lock/pyproject.toml/install_deps.py/Dockerfile, none of which had moved). Editing the Dockerfile re-keys that scope and forces the cold build that fixes it, and a fresh base refreshes every other OS package too. security-floors.txt is a PEP 508 Python floors file and cannot express a Debian package at all. The Dockerfile's own header names this exact procedure as the way to bump.
data.costIfWrong: A base-image bump moves every Debian package at once, so an unrelated OS regression would land with this ship. Mitigated by verifying Python is 3.13.15 on both digests, pip's vendored floors are unchanged, and the 16 base-image pin tests pass; CI's full Quality gate is the arbiter before merge.

data.costIfWrong: The same red recurs on some future day and costs another session the same ~40 minutes of diagnosis, minus the write-up now in the Dockerfile.

data.what: Added an atomic Redis probe LEASE (SET NX EX) on top of pybreaker to satisfy exit criterion 1b, rather than relying on pybreaker's own half-open handling.
data.why: MEASURED in pybreaker 1.4.1 source: CircuitOpenState.before_call checks 'now < opened_at + timeout' and then calls half_open(), which is a PLAIN Redis SET, not a compare-and-set - so two workers past the reset timeout both pass the check and both probe. And CircuitHalfOpenState defines NO before_call override, so while the shared state reads half-open EVERY arriving call executes the provider call. pybreaker therefore provides no single-probe guarantee across processes; CircuitRedisStorage shares state but does not serialize the probe. The plan says 'exactly one probe allowed even with two workers', which cannot be met by pybreaker alone.
data.costIfWrong: If the lease TTL is shorter than a provider call, a second worker could probe while the first is still in flight; mitigated by deriving the TTL from worst_case_call_seconds() so the lease outlives the call it guards.

data.what: pybreaker's call_async is UNUSABLE here: in 1.4.1 it is a Tornado @gen.coroutine, not asyncio. The plan's Read-first says 'use call_async around the coroutine'; that instruction is wrong for this version. The breaker instead awaits the coroutine itself and reports the verdict to the library through its PUBLIC sync call().
data.why: Measured: calling breaker.call_async(factory) raises NameError: name 'gen' is not defined, because pybreaker imports tornado.gen behind HAS_TORNADO_SUPPORT and tornado is not installed (nor should it be in a FastAPI/asyncio service). The obvious alternative, breaker.call(factory), is worse-than-useless: it would invoke the coroutine FUNCTION, receive a coroutine OBJECT, and record a SUCCESS without ever awaiting it - so a provider outage would never be counted and the breaker would never open, while looking like working code. Reporting the awaited outcome through call() keeps every transition (counting, open, half-open, close) owned by the library.
data.costIfWrong: If pybreaker changes call()'s bookkeeping the verdict shape could drift; mitigated because _report uses only the public call() and the tests red-prove the counting (M3: removing failure reporting = 6 reds).

data.what: Rewrote the exit-1b test to make the two probes CONCURRENT after discovering the sequential version was a false gate.
data.why: Red-proof caught it: with the probe lease deleted the original sequential test still passed 11/11. Reason: worker one's FAILURE re-opens the breaker with a fresh opened_at, so the window check - not the lease - refused worker two. The test pinned the window and claimed to pin the lease. The concurrent version admits both workers before either completes, which is the real shape (two Celery workers taking turns at the same instant) and the only shape the lease answers. With it, deleting the lease produces exactly 1 red.
data.costIfWrong: None known: the concurrent test subsumes the sequential one, and the window check retains its own red-proof (M2 = 3 reds).
